extracted.intended_audience: UK civil servants and policy officials drafting or running public consultations
extracted.subtask_description: Practical principles for designing, timing, publishing and responding to UK government public consultations to ensure they are accessible, targeted, informative and have practical impact on policy. Focuses on process and quality standards for consultation documents and management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations should be clear and concise
rubrics_metrics.description: Use plain English and avoid acronyms. Be clear what questions you are asking and limit the number of questions to those that are necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make consultations easy to understand and easy to answer. Avoid lengthy documents when possible and consider merging those on related topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations should have a purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not consult for the sake of it; consult at a formative stage of policy or implementation planning and take responses into account when taking policy forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask departmental lawyers whether you have a legal duty to consult. Do not ask questions about issues on which you already have a final view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations should be informative
rubrics_metrics.description: Give enough information to ensure consultees understand the issues and can give informed responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include validated impact assessments of costs and benefits of options when possible; this may be required where proposals impact business or the voluntary sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations are only part of a process of engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise consultation as one element in ongoing engagement rather than the only method of engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider informal iterative consultation, using new digital tools and open, collaborative approaches. Consultation is not just about formal documents and responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations should last for a proportionate amount of time
rubrics_metrics.description: Set consultation length based on legal advice and the nature and impact of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid consulting for too long (which delays policy) and avoid consulting too quickly (which reduces response quality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations should be targeted
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the full range of people, businesses and voluntary bodies affected and whether representative groups exist; target specific groups where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure affected groups are aware of and can access the consultation. Tailor methods to needs/preferences of particular groups (e.g., older people, younger people, people with disabilities) who may not respond to traditional methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations should take account of the groups being consulted
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult stakeholders in ways that suit them, recognising differing capacities and constraints among consultees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow charities more time than businesses if needed. If consultation spans holiday periods, consider mitigating actions such as prior discussion with key parties or extending the consultation deadline beyond the holiday period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations should be agreed before publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek collective agreement before publishing a written consultation, particularly for new policy proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation should facilitate scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Make responses and government reactions transparent and easy to find.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish any response on the same gov.uk page as the original consultation; make clear when the government has responded; explain what responses were received and how they informed policy; state how many responses were received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government responses to consultations should be published in a timely fashion
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish responses within 12 weeks of the consultation or explain why this is not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where consultation concerns a statutory instrument, publish responses before or at the same time as the instrument is laid except in very exceptional circumstances (and even then publish as soon as possible). Allow appropriate time between closing the consultation and implementing policy or legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation exercises should not generally be launched during local or national election periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid launching consultations during election periods unless absolutely essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If exceptional circumstances make a consultation essential (for example, safeguarding public health), departments should seek advice from the Propriety and Ethics team in the Cabinet Office.
